chapter: New Orleans musicians, recordings and radio
title: Traveling tourist class and dressing by Patou and Saks
summary: She traveled tourist, spending on stage clothes made by Patou in Europe and Saks Fifth Avenue shops at home, but dressing plainly off stage.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Did you ever perform on the ships that you --

Listen, I was always -- I never did want to spend -- first of all, Chris, I didn't -- when I was on the stage, I wanted to come out with some smart clothes on that nobody had had on but me. I'd see to that, because Patou dressed me when I was in Europe, you know, most of the time.

But in America here I'd go to Saks Fifth Avenue. You know, they have those women that have their shops, like the smart individual shops, you know, and the women that had those shops, they would put -- dress me. And I always wore beautiful clothes on the stage.

Off the stage I was sorry jeans didn't come out before, because I liked to be just plainly dressed on the street. My clothes were always good, but plain for the street, you know? But on the stage I never could wear anything under my clothes, because they were always very slinky and formfitting. See? So that's how it was on the stage.
But look at me now -- my shopping bag, you know? That's what I like.
